title: The Community Rule (1QS), translated by G. Vermes, col. III: the two spirits
authors: Vermes, G. (translator)
venue: CCAT (ccat.sas.upenn.edu), University of Pennsylvania; course text file '1QS'
ask_addressed: Read and quote the Dead Sea Scrolls themselves from open translations or scholarly pages (Community Rule, War Scroll, Damascus Document, Pesher Habakkuk, Temple Scroll, Copper Scroll, Great Isaiah Scroll and Cave 4 biblical manuscripts as witnesses to the Hebrew Bible)
quote: by the Prince of Light and walk in the ways of light, but all the children of falsehood are ruled
summary: Treatise on the Two Spirits as Vermes translates it: God appoints two spirits, truth and falsehood; the children of righteousness are ruled by the Prince of Light, the children of falsehood by the Angel of Darkness. The page is a translation only, with no apparatus or Hebrew.
limits: Translation date not printed on the page. Composition is not dated here: the Iranica date is for the sect's founding and the hand date is for a copy. Hempel's abstract (page 21) says the Treatise was probably incorporated into the Rule late. Says nothing on who wrote it. Correction by verifier: the researcher's note that 1QS was not radiocarbon-dated in Jull et al. was wrong; Table 2 dates it. copy: unauthorised-looking upload; cite the publication, not this URL.

text.locator: III 20-21 (within the Treatise on the Two Spirits, from III 13; the page numbers the lines)
text.edition: G. Vermes translation as posted on CCAT (Penn), file '1QS'; the page names Vermes and prints no publication details

composition.basis: No source I opened dates the composition of the Treatise or of 1QS. Iranica (Duchesne-Guillemin 1994) says only that the sect was founded in the mid-2nd c. BCE; the c. 100-75 BCE hand is a copy date (Jull et al. 1995, App. 1). Hempel (2010, abstract) argues the Treatise was probably incorporated into the Rule at a late stage.

text.witness: 1QS from Cave 1, hand c. 100-75 BCE (Cross, quoted in Jull et al. 1995, App. 1); radiocarbon on 1QS (sample DSS-4, AA-13418): 2041 +/- 68 BP, 2-sigma 206 BC-AD 111 (98%) (Jull et al. 1995, Table 2). 4Q258 (Cave 4 copy): script 'beginning of the first century BC' (Cross, in Jull et al.), radiocarbon-dated too.

title: Radiocarbon Dating of Scrolls and Linen Fragments from the Judean Desert
authors: Jull, A. J. T.; Donahue, D. J.; Broshi, M.; Tov, E.
ask_addressed: Give the discovery (1946-47, Cave 1) and the dating evidence: radiocarbon (Jull et al. 1995, Radiocarbon 37; Bonani 1992), palaeography, and the competing readings of who wrote them (Essene hypothesis vs Golb's Jerusalem-library theory vs others)
quote: The radiocarbon results are in good agreement with estimates of age based on paleography.
summary: AMS dates on 18 texts and 2 linen pieces (Arizona) fit the palaeographic dates except the first sample of 4Q258; 1QIsaa at 2141 +/- 32 BP agrees with the earlier Zurich value. Two documentary texts, 4Q342 and 4Q344, are dated as late as Bar-Kokhba and thought mixed in by dealers (Broshi).
limits: Measures the age of parchment, not of composition. Calibration and sample-cleaning issues (castor oil on some parchments) are raised in Rodley and Thiering 1999, which discusses Doudna's 1998 reanalysis. Authors are affiliated with the Israel Museum Shrine of the Book (Broshi) and the Dead Sea Scrolls Publication Project (Tov), which supplied the samples; no conflict statement on the page. Verifier: the 'first sample of 4Q258' exception is on the page; Table 2 also gives 1QS (DSS-4) and 4Q266 results.

title: The Origins of the Dead Sea Scrolls
authors: Golb, N.
venue: Fathom Archive, University of Chicago (excerpt of Scribner 1995)

quote: Taken from Jerusalem libraries and personal collections at a crucial hour and hidden away in many places in the wilderness
summary: Golb's thesis in his own words: the Scrolls are remains of Jerusalem libraries and private collections hidden in the Judaean Wilderness before 70 CE, not a sectarian library; he also says the 'Qumran-Essene hypothesis had become a fact in the minds of the editors' and points to over fifty hands in Cave 1.

Verifier: Golb's page says only 'the time of the First Revolt'; the years 66-70 CE are given for this thesis on the ASOR blog page (candidate 19), not on this page.
